claims.text: Python's standard library includes the time module, which provides Unix‑time timestamps for messages.
JavaScript's built‑in Date object supplies millisecond‑resolution timestamps based on the Unix epoch.
Java's standard library offers the Instant class, which holds Unix timestamps with second and nanosecond precision.

evidence.quote: Python provides a time library which uses Unix time. JavaScript provides a Date library which provides and stores timestamps in milliseconds since the Unix epoch and is implemented in all modern desktop and mobile web browsers as well as in JavaScript server environments like Node.js
Java provides an Instant object which holds a Unix timestamp in both seconds and nanoseconds
The C standard library uses Unix time for all date and time functions, and Unix time is sometimes referred to as time_t, the name of the data type used for timestamps in C and C++
